column1: # Reviewed function extents that correct the Ghidra dump — consumed by tools/split.py.
# The dump's sizes for some Sony-built (EE GCC) functions run into the next function (24-byte
# functions recorded as 32) or stop short of the closing `jr ra` + delay slot. A row's size is the
# extent the retail bytes show (the EE GCC 2.96 object of the matching C source, or the body walk in
# tools/split.py `_sweep_extent`, checked against the retail bytes by tools/verify.py). split.py
# accepts a row only when it never cuts into another function: a growth must stop at the next
# function; a plain shrink must leave nothing but zero words (alignment nops) before the next
# function. Two reviewed keywords in the fourth column go further (docs/engine/function-inventory.md):
#   cut    the shrink leaves code behind — the dump glued a second function onto this one. The
#          remainder is claimed by a promotion rule (a `j`/`jal` target, a referenced start or a framed
#          body); split.py refuses the run if nothing claims it, so a cut never orphans code.
#   merge  the function at <va> takes <size> and the row's name, absorbing every dump function that
#          starts inside that extent (Ghidra split one 40-byte leaf into a `thunk_` and a fragment).
# --- EE GCC sizes verified by the matching C source (tools/verify.py) ---------------------------
# --- epilogues the dump stopped short of: the `ld`/`lwc1` restores, `jr ra` and its delay slot
# --- lie after the recorded end (inventory audit, 160 asm bodies in the EE GCC blocks; the
# --- extent is the body walk's, every added word is the function's own epilogue) -------------
# --- two functions under one symbol: the head keeps the bytes up to its own return or tail call,
# --- the second function is promoted by the rule its evidence satisfies --------------------------
# tail-call wrapper; the dump swallowed the first word of the framed body after it
# span reaches the referenced leaf at 0x155490
# span reaches the referenced leaf at 0x159a70
# wrapper tail-calls the framed body at 0x17c8a0 (near-miss-shapes-extents.md)
# jump-table growth reached the referenced 16-byte wrapper at 0x1b68b0 (DAT_001b68b0 in FUN_001a44d0)
# wrapper tail-calls the framed body at the j target
# the 8-byte getter at 0x267490 (jal target of FUN_0026c3c8) is its own function
# data/function-extents.json span reaches the vtable-referenced leaf at 0x2d3f60
# span reaches the referenced leaf at 0x2efc40
# 8-byte `j` wrapper; the referenced 12-byte leaf at 0x453a30 is its own function

# the head ends in a `j` to a leaf body (no frame) that follows it under the same symbol; the body is a
# separate function the wrapper tail-calls (rule 3 claims it)
